answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may endorse a claim, then cap each stake’s influence and slash it when an independent audit proves the endorsement was fabricated. A crystal-clear audit trail links each endorsement to its deposit, while a thread of randomly selected reviewers checks claims across a trellis of distinct accounts. Creating many Sybils then requires locking real capital in every account, and getting caught destroys part of that capital, making mass deception costly rather than merely a matter of generating names.
